No firing, injuries, technical cutaway, assembly, repair, instructions or operating steps. Western Han China, around the second to first century BCE. A single adult Han foot soldier, wearing a modest dark brown lamellar vest over a charcoal cross-collared tunic, trousers, cloth cap and simple footwear, sits quietly on a low stone bench at the open doorway of an earthen storehouse. The principal subject is a complete recognizable ancient WOODEN CROSSBOW resting safely sideways across his lap, with its broad transverse wooden bow and long wooden stock all clearly visible. It is in a relaxed unstrung storage state, with no arrow on it; a loose bowstring rests separately on folded linen on a small bench beside him. His two hands rest lightly on the stock and his knee, not demonstrating the mechanism. Small bronze rear fittings are modest period accents rather than a detailed mechanism illustration. Whole head, two arms and two feet visible, natural coherent anatomy. A plain basket, rolled reed mat and a few closed storage containers add the sense of Han military stores. No other weapons, no archery target, no dramatic pose. Elevated front three-quarter composition, warm afternoon light. Clothing, wooden form, bronze fittings and setting are an imaginative period example, not a replica of a named excavated artifact.
